name: Congo Free State
alt: Congo Free State under Leopold II

predecessors.name: International Association of the Congo
predecessors.text: the lower Congo and Stanley Pool, where Stanley built a road 'from the lower Congo up to Stanley Pool' (August 1879 to June 1884)

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Kongo
predecessors.text: the Congo-side lands of the Kongo, 'assimilated into ... the Independent State of the Congo'

successors.name: Belgian Congo
successors.text: the whole Congo plus the Lado Enclave

ledger.x: 1885 July: the Congo Free State is created.
1887 (bridge): the Congolese part of the Lunda heartland passes to the Free State.
1887 February 24: Tippu Tip accepts the governorship of the Stanley Falls District.
1889 (bridge): the Luba empire splits and 'later joined the Congo Free State'.
1891 December: the Stairs expedition takes Katanga.
1892 March: Sefu bin Hamid attacks the Free State.
1894: the Lado Enclave is leased to Leopold.
1894 January: the last Arab-Swahili forts surrender.
1894 January: Maniema is under the Free State.
1908 November 15: Belgium annexes the Congo Free State.

wars.name: Stairs Expedition to Katanga
wars.outcome: The Free State's Stairs Expedition reached Bunkeya on 14 December 1891 (Msiri page) and Msiri was killed on 20 December (Yeke infobox); Katanga passed to the Free State.

wars.name: Congo Arab war
wars.outcome: Free State victory: Nyangwe fell on 4 March 1893, Kasongo on 22 April 1893, Sefu died on 20 October 1893 and the last forts surrendered in January 1894.

wars.name: Congo Free State against the Mahdists (Rejaf)
wars.outcome: Dhanis' column mutinied in February 1897 and Chaltin's force won the Battle of Rejaf on 17 February 1897; the page gives no territorial result.

certainty.note: Recognised on paper at Berlin; effective control was the river and the stations.
The boundary treaties with Portugal, France and the United Kingdom (1885-1894) are not dated by the pages opened, so no frontier is drawn sharp.
